title: Safe complete splitting with protected edges in an enhanced graph

standard_prerequisites.name: Frank–Mader splitting theorem
standard_prerequisites.permitted_use: Existence of a complete split preserving edge connectivity before imposing the protected-edge constraint. The new constraint is proved here; the theorem is not taken to prove it.

standard_prerequisites.name: edge-cut identities
standard_prerequisites.permitted_use: Counting identity and submodularity; the source proof also writes its elementary partition identity explicitly.

core_obligations: Choose a connectivity-preserving complete split with the minimum number of invalid protected-edge pairs.
Use the enhanced-graph degree budget to find an unprotected pair, then compare the two crossed pairings.
If both crossed operations destroy connectivity, obtain crossing cuts of sizes k or k+1; exploit even k, parity of intersection cuts and the remaining xy edge to contradict submodularity.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the ordinary graph case by Mader; choose a minimum-invalid complete split in the enhanced case.
Find four half-edges and two candidate repairs; derive crossing cuts if both repairs fail.
Exclude the two k+1 cuts by parity, then exclude the remaining k/k+1 case by the cut identity.

difficulty_reason: Even after the standard splitting theorem is granted, preserving the protected-edge structure requires a minimum-defect pairing choice, two competing rewiring operations and a parity-sensitive uncrossing contradiction. The special vertex has an exceptional connectivity allowance, so the proof must show the relevant cut regions contain ordinary vertices before applying the k lower bound. This is the source-specific remaining argument, rather than an immediate application of Menger or Mader.

compared.difference: The published item concerns the K5-immersion application in the internally 4-edge-connected setting. This task is the protected-edge safe complete split for arbitrary even k; same paper but distinct hypotheses and conclusion.

dedup.scope: Same-source old primary inspected. Global related-claim comparison and exclusion-list confirmation remain for integration; no uniqueness certification inferred from different labels.

assembly.notes: Use original asset basename valid-ops.pdf. Preserve all selected native mathematical text and source labels. The standard theorem is printed as an uncounted input; the local definitions, cut identity and figure accompany the counted complete-split lemma.

open_scientific_issues.identified_by: root independent review; confirmed by B
open_scientific_issues.example: Two vertices u and u-prime, k parallel edges, u special, F empty. The graph satisfies enhanced/nearly-k-connected assumptions and u-prime has degree k, but every pair at u-prime lies in delta(u), so every split is invalid.
open_scientific_issues.root_cause: Source356 applies d({u,u-prime})>=k even when this is the entire vertex set with empty boundary. No preceding global >=3-vertex restriction was found in the original definitions/section.
open_scientific_issues.scope: Hold this standalone claim. Do not infer that the whole main splitter theorem is false; do not silently add a new hypothesis.

editorial_scope: One new counted lemma. Original source and author proof are retained; the standard Frank–Mader result and source-local definitions are uncounted prerequisites. No original mathematical statement or proof is rewritten.
